clues.clue: Sworn in January 2026 as the 112th mayor of New York City, this democratic socialist is the city's first Muslim mayor.
clues.reveal: Zohran Mamdani. The 112th mayor of New York City, sworn in January 1, 2026, succeeding Eric Adams; a former Queens assembly member.

clues.clue: The mayor heads this branch of city government, responsible for running agencies and enforcing local law.
clues.reveal: Executive. The mayor leads the executive branch, overseeing the agencies that deliver city services.

clues.clue: Term limits cap the mayor, council members, and other city elected officials at this many consecutive terms.
clues.reveal: Two. New York City term limits restrict most elected officials to two consecutive four-year terms.
clues.src_title: Term limits in New York City

clues.clue: The New York City Council has this many members, each representing a district of about 170,000 people.
clues.reveal: 51. The City Council has 51 members, each elected from a single district.

clues.clue: This council leader, Julie Menin as of 2026, sets the legislative agenda and is the body's most powerful member.
clues.reveal: Speaker. The Speaker (Julie Menin as of 2026) leads the City Council and controls its agenda.

clues.clue: The Council can override a mayoral veto with a vote of this fraction of its members.
clues.reveal: Two-thirds. A two-thirds vote of the Council can override the mayor's veto of legislation.

clues.clue: This founding document is essentially New York City's constitution, setting up its government and powers.
clues.reveal: City Charter. The New York City Charter is the city's governing document, defining its structure and powers.

clues.clue: Changes to the Charter are studied by a temporary commission, then must be approved by the voters this way.
clues.reveal: Referendum. Charter changes proposed by a Charter Revision Commission go to the voters as ballot referenda.

clues.clue: A 1989 ruling forced a charter rewrite by abolishing this powerful body that had shared budget and land use power.
clues.reveal: Board of Estimate. The Supreme Court found it unconstitutional in 1989, prompting a major charter revision that empowered the City Council.
clues.src_title: New York City Board of Estimate

clues.clue: This citywide official is the city's chief financial officer and auditor, a watchdog over its budget.
clues.reveal: Comptroller. The elected city Comptroller audits agencies and manages the city's finances and pension funds.

clues.clue: Next in line to the mayor, this citywide watchdog also fields complaints about city agencies.
clues.reveal: Public Advocate. First in line of succession to the mayor, the Public Advocate is a citywide ombudsman.

clues.clue: Each of the five boroughs elects one of these officials, who appoints community board members and advises on land use.
clues.reveal: Borough President. Each borough elects a president who appoints community board members and weighs in on land use and budget.
